text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- British Prime Minister John Major and caretaker Prime Minister Meraj Khalid held preliminary talks, focusing on ways to promote trade and investment between the two countries.

- Shahid Javed Burki, adviser to the caretaker Prime Minister on Finance and Economic Affairs, said the present regime was pursuing a three-faceted strategy of stabilisation, structural reforms and poverty alleviation to revitalise the sagging economy.

- The Supreme Court has held that the Eighth Amendment was a valid part of the Constitution and Article 58(2), giving power to the president to dissolve the National Assembly (lower house), was a deterrent to the imposition of martial law.
- The government has decided to deploy 250,000 troops on election day (February 3) to maintain law and order and perform election duties, says caretaker Defence Minister Shahid Hamid.

- President Farooq Leghari has said if the Supreme Court restored the previous government the election process would come to an end. But, he added, there is a very strong case for the previous government not to be restored.

- Amounts required for debt servicing and defence will be deducted from federal government resources before determining the divisible pool for distribution among the federation and the provinces in line with the National Finance Commission Award.
- Government-owned banks and development finance institutions have been asked to submit plans to reduce their work force by 30 percent by January 15.

- The government has finalised details of the new gold policy under which the import of gold and diamonds would be allowed free of customs duty, sales tax, surcharge and advance income tax and withholding tax against the export performance of an exporter.
- Rival Afghan factions are meeting in Islamabad on Monday to negotiate an immediate ceasefire and formation of a technical working group.
